title: Provisioning: dashboards + alerts for time-to-ready and stage breakdown
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes:
- Adds Dedicated provisioning readiness dashboard with stage breakdown and per-run drilldowns
- Adds alert rules for stuck stages, high failure rate, and time-to-ready regression
- Adds standardized template variables for pool/customer/region and links to runbooks
description: Context: Provision-to-ready automation sprint needs a single place to understand (a) where provisioning runs are spending time and (b) when to page vs ticket for automation failures. This PR adds Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert rules for provisioning stages and the end-to-end time-to-ready metric emitted by the control plane. It also standardizes template variables for pool/customer and fixes template variable population for newly-created pool IDs (INT-1045). Includes low-cardinality guidance and safe defaults to avoid exploding series when filtering by run_id/correlation_id. Rollout: ship dashboards immediately; keep paging alerts behind a routing label until SRE confirms thresholds after the staging pilot. Related: ENG-2748 (structured events + metrics), ENG-2749 (dashboard), ENG-2756 (baseline backfill).
commits: dashboards: add dedicated provisioning overview (time-to-ready + stage breakdown)
alerts: add stuck-stage + failure-rate alerts (non-paging by default)
alerts: add time-to-ready p95 regression alert (paging behind label gate)
grafana: standardize template vars (pool_id/customer_id/region) and fix pool dropdown query
docs: add panel links to runbooks + control-plane troubleshooting
body:
What: Add dashboards + alerts for Dedicated provisioning runs (provision-to-ready) and standardize template variables for pool/customer. Dashboards:
- Dedicated > Provisioning Readiness (Overview)
  - Time-to-ready: p50/p95 by region and sku (where available)
  - Stage duration histograms: Requested→Provisioning→Imaging→Bootstrapping→Validating→Ready/Failed
  - Failure rate by stage + top error_category
  - "Runs" table with correlation_id/run_id, current stage, elapsed time, last error, and deep links
- Dedicated > Provisioning Run (Drilldown)
  - Per-run timeline (stage start/finish events)
  - Logs/traces links via correlation_id
  - Key health checks summary: gpu_health, dns, tls, runtime_smoke, perf_canary
- Dedicated > Stage Breakdown
  - Stage duration heatmap by region + pool_id
  - Retry counts + retry reason buckets

Alerts (Prometheus rules):
- provisioning_stage_stuck (ticket by default; optional paging)
  - Triggers when a run stays in the same stage > threshold (default thresholds below)
- provisioning_stage_failure_rate_high (ticket)
  - Triggers on elevated stage failure rate over 30m for a region (rate-based)
- provisioning_time_to_ready_p95_regression (paging gated)
  - Triggers when p95 time-to-ready exceeds target for 2h (label-gated route)
- provisioning_slo_burn (ticket initially)
  - Error-budget style burn alert, aligned to proposed readiness SLO

Default thresholds (can be overridden via values.yaml):
- Provisioning: 45m
- Imaging: 90m (with known variance by region)
- Bootstrapping: 60m
- Validating: 45m
- End-to-end time-to-ready p95: 6h (pilot target; subject to tuning)

Template variables (Grafana):
- customer_id (from provisioning metrics label; fallback to control-plane pool registry metric)
- pool_id
- region
- sku (optional; only present when emitted)
- stage

Cardinality safety:
- run_id/correlation_id are only used in the drilldown dashboard and are not used in alert grouping.
- Alerts group by {region, stage} by default; pool_id grouping is optional and disabled by default.

Runbook links:
- Panels include links to Dedicated pool provisioning runbook and control-plane ready-state troubleshooting; links use a shared lib so we can update once.

Why: Operators need to see where time is being spent and whether we are failing for infra vs validation vs control-plane registration. Sales/CS also needs predictable lead-time reporting; this dashboard becomes the shared artifact for stage budgets and pilot retros.

How to test:
1) In staging, load the "Provisioning Readiness (Overview)" dashboard.
2) Set customer_id + pool_id to an internal pilot pool.
3) Validate that:
   - Stage duration panels populate
   - Runs table shows correlation_id
   - Drilldown links resolve and keep variables
4) Validate rules load via promtool (CI does this) and that alerts stay non-paging unless routing label is set.

Notes:
- INT-1045: fixes pool_id dropdown not populating for new pools by switching the variable query to use the pool registry metric as a source of truth (and joining where possible), rather than relying on a stage metric that may not exist yet.
- Requires metrics emitted in control plane PRs (ENG-2748). If a pool has only partial metrics, panels will show "No data" instead of misleading zeros.

Follow-ups (not in this PR):
- Add a lightweight "customer view" dashboard with fewer operator-specific panels (Lauren requested for CS).
- Tune stuck-stage thresholds once we have a week of staging data.
- Decide whether to page on SLO burn vs only page on stuck stages; initial routing is conservative to avoid noise.
conversation: Allison Grant (reviewer): Dashboard looks good overall. Two asks: (1) can we avoid grouping any alerts by pool_id by default to reduce cardinality, and (2) please standardize the variable names across all three dashboards (customer_id/pool_id/region).
Sergio Costa (author): Ack. Updated alert rules to group by {region, stage} only, and added a shared templating lib for customer_id/pool_id/region. Pushed follow-up commit and updated snapshots.
Aisha Bello (reviewer): For time-to-ready p95 regression, can we gate paging? We’re still debating thresholds and don’t want a new page source during pilot week.
Sergio Costa (author): Yep. Added a label gate `severity=page` that is off by default; values.yaml defaults to `severity=ticket`. We can flip once SRE signs off.

Logan Wright (reviewer): For the pool_id variable query: please ensure it returns pools even before the first provisioning event lands (this was the INT-1045 complaint). Also make sure the panel links preserve variables when jumping to drilldown.

Sergio Costa (author): Fixed by sourcing pool_id list from `control_plane_pool_registry_info` and using that as the dropdown source; stage metrics are only used after selection. Also switched drilldown links to use `var-pool_id=${pool_id}` style params; verified in staging with a newly created pool.

Rafael Mendes (reviewer): Alert thresholds: Bootstrapping at 60m seems right, Imaging 90m is ok but we should include a note about known regional variance. Also please add runbook links in alert annotations.
Sergio Costa (author): Added variance note in dashboard README and included runbook URLs in alert annotations (provisioning runbook + ready-state troubleshooting).
Allison Grant (reviewer): Approving after last CI run is green. Please keep CHANGELOG entry concise.
Sergio Costa (author): Squashed + updated CHANGELOG. Ready to merge.
System: All checks passed. PR merged via squash by Connor O'Brien.
